summary: This tutorial details the implementation of a stateful, identity-agnostic weather integration within the 'riff' voice application. It addresses the challenge of persisting user preferences (specifically home city) across sessions without relying on authenticated caller IDs, utilizing a local JSON-backed preference store and a self-contained Open-Meteo API flow.
title: Weather Integration and Global Preferences

summary: This tutorial details the implementation of a 'Grounding Integrity Gate' within the Riff codebase, addressing critical production failures caused by non-deterministic conversational flows and rigid telephony routing. By introducing a phased validation pipeline (Static through OTA) backed by a kill switch, and decoupling phone routing via a JSON-backed preference store, the system achieves deterministic state management and granular per-number flow assignment.
title: Grounding Integrity Gate

summary: This tutorial addresses the challenge of testing audio-gated conversational flows in text-only environments. It details how to decouple flow logic from audio playback dependencies by simulating engine events and filtering configuration artifacts, enabling robust text-mode debugging for voice-first applications.
title: Web Audio-Gated Flows and Flow Picker

summary: This tutorial details the architectural shift in the 'riff' project from Anthropic Haiku to Alibaba DashScope (Qwen) for default utterance generation. It demonstrates how to implement a vendor-agnostic LLM client using standard library tools to minimize dependency bloat, while maintaining backward compatibility with existing providers through a unified Persona interface.
title: Alibaba DashScope/Qwen Integration

summary: This tutorial outlines a Test-Driven Development (TDD) framework for evaluating autonomous agent flows. By leveraging LLM-driven personas to simulate human interactions and a separate judge model to score outcomes, developers can systematically grade task success, quality, and robustness. The approach distinguishes between infrastructure failures and logical flow errors, supporting both offline stubbed testing and live execution modes.
title: Flow Evaluation
